findings.title: Rockwell Automation Logix Controllers (Update A) - CISA ICS Advisory ICSA-21-056-03
findings.summary_md: CISA's ICS advisory for CVE-2021-22681, originally published February 25, 2021 and revised March 18, 2021. It documents the verification-key authentication bypass in RSLogix 5000 and Studio 5000 Logix Designer affecting CompactLogix, ControlLogix, DriveLogix, GuardLogix and SoftLogix controllers, co-discovered by researchers at Soonchunhyang University, Kaspersky, and Claroty (Sharon Brizinov and Tal Keren). Rockwell determined the vulnerability cannot be mitigated with a patch and recommended network segmentation, blocking TCP 44818 from outside the ICS network zone, CIP Security deployment, and monitoring of controller change logs.

findings.title: NVD detail record for CVE-2021-22681
findings.summary_md: The NVD entry for CVE-2021-22681, published March 3, 2021 and last modified June 17, 2026, describes the flaw in Rockwell Studio 5000 Logix Designer and RSLogix 5000 where a key used to verify Logix controller communications can be bypassed. It maps the issue to CWE-522 (Insufficiently Protected Credentials) and cites CISA advisory ICSA-21-056-03 and the KEV catalog as references. The June 2026 modification shows the record was still being maintained weeks before the water-sector campaign began.

findings.title: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog entry for CVE-2021-22681
findings.summary_md: CISA added CVE-2021-22681 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on March 5, 2026 with a required-action due date of March 26, 2026 under BOD 22-01, citing an insufficient protected credentials vulnerability in multiple Rockwell products. The entry states the Logix Designer key can be discovered, letting an unauthorized application connect to Logix controllers from the network. It links the Rockwell support advisory (answer 1130301), ICSA-21-056-03, and NVD as sources.
